text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Galeforce winds and ice causing traffic problems throughout the country.
- Some $150 million should be invested in the Koncar group by the year 2001 in order to modernise tehnology and equipment.
- Confectioner Kras's wholesale trade has gone up by 45.7 percent in 1996 in a year-on-year comparison with 1995, while retail sales went up 16.7 percent during the same period.
- The implementation of the law on denationalisation to commence on January 1, when requests for purchase of flats can be submitted.
- 28,000 Croat expatriots have returned to Croatia, according to the newly set up immigration ministry. Another 3,5 million Croats still living out of Croatia.

- Slovenia planning to, at the beginning of 1997, reduce the quantity of electricity sent to Croatia and produced by the Krsko Slovene-Croatian nuclear plant (NEK), due to the plant's troubled finances.
- Interview with Branko Borkovic, president of the Croatian War Veterans' Association: Our rights have not been clearly stated. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
